texts: mixed: the lighting event, both Harbor Row possessives, sundown and Year 1 all come through, and "together" is doing real work — it is what suppresses the per-keeper distribution rule, which is the collective reading, even though the word itself gets no atom. The one real shortfall is "day 300 of Year 1": the translator's day term is the day-within-a-month slot and it has no day-of-year term, so the number is recorded in a slot that means something else. No rewrite preserves a day-of-year count, so leave the sentence as it stands unless your calendar can supply a month — "On the twelfth day of Thawmonth in Year 1, the keepers of the Harbor Row together lit the lanterns of the Harbor Row at sundown." parses fully.
good. a past burning with the lanterns as the agent and mire-essence as what is consumed, plus a fireable per-lantern rule so each lantern's own burning is derivable.

good. the producing parses with the lanterns acting as one unit (no per-lantern rule, which is what "together" buys you) and mist-light as what they make; the bare "mist-light" correctly stays the class symbol here, which only becomes a problem when sentence 5 points back at it.

good. the showing, the night time-slot and a fireable per-lantern rule all come through; as in sentence 3 the bare object "mist-light" stays the class symbol, which is right for a bare mass but leaves sentence 5's definite with nothing specific to attach to.

bad: "The mist-light" points back at the light the lanterns made, but the parse fills it with the bare class symbol for mist-light in general, so a specific thing is named by a kind symbol and the light that drew the moths is never tied to the light that was produced. Fix it at first mention, by letting sentences 3 and 4 introduce the light as a thing rather than a bare mass: "Together, the lanterns produced a mist-light." and "The lanterns showed the mist-light at night." Sentence 5 then parses correctly exactly as written, with all three mentions landing on one symbol.
good. a crowd witness whose members are nightmoths, gathering as one unit at the Harbor Row — collective, so no per-moth rule, which is right for "gather".
good. the three cats parse as a counted group descending from the cliff-spires, with a fireable per-cat rule alongside the group event.

good. the hunt parses with the three cats as agents, the crowd as what is hunted, and a per-cat rule; note that "at the Harbor Row" was read as locating the crowd rather than the hunt, which the repeat of the same phrase in the next sentence supports.
good. the shrinking attaches to the same crowd introduced earlier, with the crowd as the thing that changes.
good. the survivors parse as their own group of nightmoths with the hunt as what they came through, plus a fireable per-moth rule.
good. the flight reuses the survivor group and records the Hollows as where they fled to, with a per-moth rule.
good. the arrival reuses the same survivors and the same Hollows symbol, so the fleeing and the reaching join up.
good. the molting is tied to the hunt by a during relation, with the cats as the ones that change and a fireable per-cat rule.

mixed: "The nightmoths" was resolved to the survivors — the moths that had just fled to and reached the Hollows — rather than to the crowd at the lanterns, so the threads are credited to the narrower set and left on lanterns those moths have already abandoned. Name the crowd to pin it: "The nightmoth crowd left silken threads on the lanterns of the Harbor Row." (Separately, the threads are filed as the thing changed by the leaving rather than as the thing displaced; that is a translator-side slip and no rewrite of yours fixes it.)
